result:
Created `gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReaderAgentTest.java` with 53 test methods covering `JsonReader`'s public API, matching the existing JUnit 3 (`junit.framework.TestCase`, try/fail/catch) style used by `JsonReaderPathTest` and `JsonWriterTest`.

Coverage includes: constructor null-check, lenient flag, basic array/object/nested reading, all `next*` accessors with type-mismatch errors (`IllegalStateException`), numeric edge cases (int/long overflow, non-integral-to-int conversion, quoted numbers, numbers-as-strings), malformed-JSON cases (unterminated array/object/string, premature EOF, missing values), strict-vs-lenient behavior (unquoted/single-quoted strings, comments, NaN/Infinity, multiple top-level values, non-execute prefix), case-insensitive literals, escape sequences, `skipValue` over all token types, `close()` semantics, `getPath()`, and `toString()`.

Every non-obvious behavioral assumption (e.g., that a failed `nextInt()` doesn't consume the token, that `hasNext()` doesn't detect EOF at the top-level document scope, exact column numbers, and that this Gson version permits top-level scalars even in strict mode) was verified empirically against the compiled library before being asserted, catching and fixing 4 incorrect test expectations along the way.

Verified via:
```
defects4j compile
java -cp "$(defects4j export -p cp.test)" org.junit.runner.JUnitCore com.google.gson.stream.JsonReaderAgentTest
```
Result: `OK (53 tests)`.
